acceptance: Remote OpenSSH Unix socket is mode 0660 with the managed group before tunnel status becomes online.
A chmod preparation failure kills the tunnel and enters bounded reconnect without exposing a public TCP port.
Design, operations docs, and deterministic tests no longer claim client StreamLocalBindMask controls remote permissions.

stories.given: Local DSH and the tunnel are online
stories.goal: Open one long-lived private link on any device without entering account credentials
stories.then: The browser establishes a secure session and enters DSH, with refresh, root-relative resources, APIs, and WebSocket traffic working normally
stories.value: Use the complete currently running DSH, including realtime connections

stories.given: The public site is configured but the tunnel cannot serve DSH
stories.goal: See a clear unavailable page when local DSH or its tunnel is offline
stories.then: The VPS returns a minimal branded 503 page with a retry action and no infrastructure details
stories.value: Avoid an opaque proxy error or login prompt
stories.when: The owner opens the remote URL

exact_next_action: Implement a strict secondary SSH chmod preparation step, unit-test success/failure lifecycle, update design/docs, and rerun the real stream-local canary.

receipt.outcome: Tunnel lifecycle now removes only the dedicated stale socket, binds over strict SSH, applies mode 0660 through a fixed remote command, and reports online only after that succeeds.
remaining_risks: Production setgid group inheritance and Nginx worker connectivity remain to be proven by edge apply/status.
Public TLS, offline page, plugin install, and browser rotation remain in WI-DEPLOY-E2E.
